key_insight: A fixed hard-constraint projection layer improves a PINN’s accuracy by enforcing a local discrete approximation of the nonlinear 1D Burgers’ equation.
engineering_relevance: Hard-constraint projection could make physics-informed fluid models more reliable and less sensitive to the number and placement of physics collocation points.
method: Locally discretise Burgers’ equation with a finite-difference stencil.
Decompose the discrete equation into constraint and prediction matrices to construct a projection.
Apply a final non-trainable layer that projects PINN velocity predictions onto the discrete constraint hyperplane.
evidence_signal: On an unseen uniform grid, initial experiments report approximately one order of magnitude lower data error than a comparable PINN, alongside better PDE adherence.
watch_item: Exact enforcement applies to the local discrete approximation, not the continuous PDE; evidence is limited to initial 1D Burgers’ experiments.
paper_title: Hard Constraint Projection in a Physics Informed Neural Network (Burgers)
